Not an invoice or a forecast for production. Actual metered resource averages are recorded separately. No plan or account spending settings were changed.

limitations: Loopback HTTP inside the Railway runtime; excludes browser/Vercel/public-client network latency.
Sequential synthetic reads, not a concurrent load/capacity test or production SLA.

Supabase Sydney deployment versus private PostgreSQL 17.6 in Railway US West; different DB hardware/architecture and background load. The comparison measures these deployments, not an intrinsic provider ranking.
Only the temporary app has workers disabled; the original app and its existing workers remain unchanged.
Analytics generation and media-signing cache state naturally vary; route diagnostics and per-cohort ranges are retained.
Auth login/revocation and derived analytics publication are expected writes. No booking/guest/commercial/payment mutation, paid generation, provider delivery or retention operation is invoked.
Supabase Auth/Storage/Realtime/managed schemas and ACL/ownership configuration are not migrated by this public-schema rehearsal.
No production cutover or existing provider/RV/NO_GO acceptance is authorized by these measurements.

preparation.scope: Operator preparation, excluded from the six measured cohorts
observations: The first app configuration update used a GraphQL builder enum unsupported by the live API; Dockerfile auto-detection was retained after schema inspection.

The initial local TLS connection through the public TCP proxy rejected the certificate hostname. The operator connection was corrected to validate the pinned CA and canonical private DB hostname; certificate verification was not disabled.

Operator export/restore preparation included a timed-out export, stopped public-network restores, and an incomplete overlapping local attempt. These are preparation failures, not accepted measurement samples. The final export was recreated, restored atomically through pg_restore in the owned DB container, and checked against the source snapshot.

One successful smoke cohort per database preceded the formal campaign and is retained separately. Formal cohorts retain every attempted request and stop on unexpected status, latency or correlation failures.
